## Natural history notes

A small emerald moth characterized by pale green wings crossed by distinct white bars or wavy lines, giving it a delicate leaf-like appearance when resting. In Florida, it is found in forests, hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, gardens, and other wooded or shrubby habitats where suitable host plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on leaves of woody plants and blend into foliage, helping move shrub and tree growth into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
